context.intent: SYNTHETIC UI EXAMPLE. Simplify project caching and error handling, rename session storage, and move invitation cleanup out of the application.
acceptedExceptions: Example accepted exception: a replacement cleanup service may run outside this repository, provided its deployed schedule is verified.

whatChanged: Tenant-aware project caching becomes slug-only caching.
Cancellation detection changes from error identity to a message pattern.
The session implementation is renamed without updating its public re-export.
The invitation cleanup job is removed; an empty-state copy file is added.

inspected: Illustrative source paths and caller relationships; no real reviewer was launched.
limits: All reviewer outcomes and attributions are simulated.

findings.title: A shared project slug returns another tenant’s cached data

severity.reasoning: A response can expose one tenant’s project data to another tenant.

likelihood.reasoning: Two tenants using a common slug such as onboarding is a routine scenario when they share a server process.

findings.whatGoesWrong: Tenant B requesting onboarding can receive the project cached by tenant A in the same server process.
findings.whyItHappens: The refactor removes tenantId from the cache key. The route supplies a tenant, but a cache hit returns before the tenant-scoped database lookup. The invalidation path repeats the same key collision.

findings.title: Timeout errors silently bypass both recovery handlers

severity.reasoning: An interrupted query or stream can remain pending without a visible recovery action.

likelihood.reasoning: Requires a non-cancellation error whose message includes timeout or abort.

findings.whatGoesWrong: A query or stream reporting “upstream timeout” is treated as intentional cancellation, hiding the error and recovery controls.
findings.whyItHappens: The classifier matches text instead of the cancellation error name. Both consumers return before recording failure, and the stream handler also skips its reconnect action.

codeViews.label: Error classifier
codeViews.explanation: The changed predicate accepts message substrings, including a server-side timeout.

codeViews.explanation: These separated early returns suppress different recovery paths in the same file.

findings.title: Removing the cleanup job may leave expired invitations indefinitely

severity.reasoning: Expired invitation data could accumulate beyond the intended retention window.

likelihood.reasoning: Depends on whether an external cleanup job has already replaced this registration.

findings.whatGoesWrong: If no replacement scheduler exists, expired invitation records remain stored beyond the documented cleanup window.
findings.whyItHappens: The patch removes the only cleanup registration visible in this example. The writer still persists invitation data. Whether the deletion is a regression depends on the deployment configuration.
